turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hi, how are you holding up?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm retired now and finally have time to fix up the deck. Where do I even begin?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Start with a good look for loose boards, popped nails and soft spots. Soft wood means rot and should be replaced first.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: There are a few soft boards near the steps, yes.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Replace those, then give the whole deck a scrub with a deck cleaner and let it dry for a couple of days.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Exactly. Pick a dry stretch of weather and apply a thin, even coat. Two thin coats beat one thick one.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Wait, I was going to do it all

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: well, maybe over two weekends instead.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's a sensible pace. Repairs and cleaning one weekend, staining the next.
